examples.knowledge_point: Integrating Trigonometric Expressions With Linear Arguments Using the Pythagorean Identities
examples.worked_solution:
From the identity  $1+\tan^2 \theta =\sec^2 \theta$ with $\theta = 3x,$ we get 

$$
\eqalign{
		1+\tan^2 (3x) &=\sec^2 (3x)\
		\tan^2 (3x) &=\sec^2 (3x) -1.
}
$$

Substituting the above into our integral gives

$$
\eqalign{
		\int 2\tan^2 (3x) \, \textrm{d}x&= 2\int \tan^2 (3x) \, \textrm{d}x\
                                                                &= 2\int \left(\sec^2 (3x) -1\right ) \, \textrm{d}x\
                                                                 &= 2\left(\int \sec^2 (3x)\, \textrm{d}x -\int1 \, \textrm{d}x\right)\
				                                &= 2\left( \dfrac{1}{3}\tan (3x) -x\right)+C\
                                                                 &= 	\dfrac{2}{3}\tan (3x) -2x+C.
	}
$$

In this case, we have to use the identity

$$
1+{cot}^{2}⁡x={csc}^{2}⁡x\,⟹\,{cot}^{2}⁡x={csc}^{2}⁡x-1.
$$

Therefore, we have

$$
\begin{aligned}{\int }_{\pi /6}^{\pi /4}\frac{{sin}^{2}⁡x}{\operatorname{cos}⁡x}\cdot \frac{{csc}^{4}⁡x-1}{{csc}^{2}⁡x+1}\,\text{d}x & ={\int }_{\pi /6}^{\pi /4}\frac{{sin}^{2}⁡x}{\operatorname{cos}⁡x}\cdot \frac{({csc}^{2}⁡x-1)({csc}^{2}⁡x+1)}{{csc}^{2}⁡x+1}\,\text{d}x \\  & ={\int }_{\pi /6}^{\pi /4}\frac{{sin}^{2}⁡x}{\operatorname{cos}⁡x}({csc}^{2}⁡x-1)\,\text{d}x \\  & ={\int }_{\pi /6}^{\pi /4}\frac{{sin}^{2}⁡x}{\operatorname{cos}⁡x}\cdot {cot}^{2}⁡x\,\text{d}x \\  & ={\int }_{\pi /6}^{\pi /4}\frac{{sin}^{2}⁡x}{\operatorname{cos}⁡x}\cdot \frac{{cos}^{2}⁡x}{{sin}^{2}⁡x}\,\text{d}x \\  & ={\int }_{\pi /6}^{\pi /4}\operatorname{cos}⁡x\,\text{d}x \\  & =\operatorname{sin}⁡x\,{|}_{\pi /6}^{\pi /4} \\  & =\operatorname{sin}⁡(\frac{\pi }{4})-\operatorname{sin}⁡(\frac{\pi }{6}) \\  & =\frac{\sqrt{2}}{2}-\frac{1}{2} \\  & =\frac{\sqrt{2}-1}{2}.\end{aligned}
$$
